finding.claim: DELETE /projects/:id deletes any project regardless of ownership. The authorized() check's boolean result is discarded, so any authenticated non-admin user can delete another user's project.
finding.source: Path parameter :id (attacker-supplied) with any authenticated non-admin session

trace.note: Calls authorized(req.user, project); return value is discarded
authorized() returns ownerId === user.id || user.isAdmin === true; never throws

finding.guards_checked: authorized() (api.js:12-14): correct logic, return value ignored, ineffective. authorize() (api.js:4-10): correct throwing check, not called on this route. No router- or route-level auth middleware visible in api.js; req.user assumed set upstream (unverified, does not mitigate). No null check on project: missing ID causes TypeError/500, not 403/404. PUT /projects/:id/name (api.js:25) correctly uses authorize().

verdict.guard_found: None effective. authorized() (api.js:12-14) returns a bool, but its result is discarded by the bare call at api.js:18, so it cannot block the delete at api.js:19. authorize() (api.js:4-10) would throw correctly but is not called on the DELETE route (only on api.js:25). No route-level or router-level auth middleware appears in api.js, and the only other files in the directory are .claude/skills markdown with no mounting code.
verdict.reason: At api.js:18 the boolean from authorized() (api.js:12-14) is discarded, so req.store.projects.delete(project.id) at api.js:19 runs for any project ID, meaning any authenticated non-admin user can delete another user's project; all trace lines 17-20 match the code.
